name: AI for Skilled Trades and Logistics
objectives: Given a section of a manual or spec sheet, use AI to explain it in plain words and check every number against the manual, with every number matching the source
For a real or practice job, write an estimate or work order that lists labor, parts, total, what is included and an expiry date, with the math checked by hand and every required part
For one real work task, draft a job safety checklist with AI and check it against the manual or an official safety source, adding anything AI missed before the work starts
After a job, write a work log entry with date, location, work done, materials, issues, next steps and photo notes, with every part included and no private customer information
Given several stops or items, plan a route and a simple load or inventory list, then check the route in a map app, with loads in reverse stop order and drive times checked
Using Apprenticeship.gov or a local program, find one apprenticeship or trade job you could apply for, and write down its requirements and how to apply

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Understanding manuals and specs with AI
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use AI to explain a technical manual or spec in plain words, then check it against the source.
This lesson builds toward: Given a section of a manual or spec sheet, you will use AI to explain it in plain words and check every number against the manual, with every number matching the source.
Manuals, spec sheets and installation guides are full of hard words. AI can explain them. Copy or type a section, or take a photo if your AI app reads pictures, and ask: "Explain this in plain words. What are the steps, what tools do I need, and what are the warnings?"
Ask follow-ups: "What does 'torque to 25 ft-lbs' mean?" or "What is the difference between a GFCI and a regular outlet?" AI is a great tutor for terms and concepts.
But the manual wins. Numbers like torque, voltage, pressure, clearances and weight limits must come from the manufacturer's manual, the code your area uses, or your supervisor. If AI and the manual disagree, follow the manual and ask your supervisor.
Step by step:
- Copy, type or photograph the manual section.
- Ask AI to explain it in plain words: steps, tools, warnings.
- Ask follow-ups about terms you do not know.
- Check every number against the manual.
- If they disagree, follow the manual and ask your supervisor.
Words to know:
- Spec sheet: a document listing the exact measurements and requirements for a product.
- Torque: how tightly something is turned, like a bolt.
- Code: official building or electrical rules an area requires.
Try it now: Find a manual for something you own (a tool, appliance or vehicle) online or in a drawer. Ask AI to explain one section in plain words, then check every number against the manual.
You can now use AI to understand manuals and specs while trusting the official numbers.

options: A sales flyer with prices
A list of exact measurements and requirements for a product
A safety poster for the break room
A customer's review of a product
check.why: A spec sheet gives the exact measurements and requirements you must meet.

check.q: AI explains a manual section but gives a voltage that is different from the manual. What would you do?
options: Use the voltage in the manual and ask your supervisor
Use the AI number because it is newer
Average the two numbers
Skip the step
check.why: Numbers like voltage come from the manual, not AI; ask your supervisor if unsure.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Writing a clear estimate or work order
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Write a professional estimate or work order with AI help.
This lesson builds toward: For a real or practice job, you will write an estimate or work order that lists labor, parts, total, what is included and an expiry date, with the math checked by hand and every required part.
Customers and supervisors trust workers who put things in writing. An estimate tells a customer what you will do and what it will cost before you start. A work order records a job: what was asked, what was done, materials used and time spent.
Tell AI the facts and let it format: "Write a simple estimate for replacing a bathroom faucet. Labor 2 hours at $60 per hour. Parts: faucet $85, supply lines $15. Valid 30 days. Customer must choose the faucet model." Check the math and every detail.
Keep it honest: list what is included and what is not, and say the price may change if you find hidden problems, with the customer's approval first. Use a free template in Google Docs or Word and save a copy of every one.
Step by step:
- Write the job, labor hours and rate, and parts with prices.
- Ask AI to format a simple estimate or work order.
- Check the math and details.
- Add what is included, what is not, and when it expires.
- Save a copy.
Words to know:
- Estimate: a written price for a job before it starts.
- Work order: a record of a job: what was asked, what was done, materials and time.
- Labor: the cost of the worker's time.
Try it now: Write an estimate for a real or practice job with AI help: labor, parts, total, what is included and an expiry date. Check the math by hand.
You can now write a clear, honest estimate or work order with AI help.

check.q: What does "parts" mean on an estimate?
options: The worker's time
The tax on the job
The materials needed for the job
The travel time
check.why: Parts are the materials; labor is the worker's time.

check.q: AI totals your estimate at $310, but your hand math says $280. What would you do?
options: Send $310 because AI is better at math
Send $280 without checking
Send both numbers to the customer
Recheck each line and send the correct total
check.why: Always check the math line by line before sending an estimate.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Making a job safety checklist
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Draft a job safety checklist with AI and check it against official safety sources.
This lesson builds toward: For one real work task, you will draft a job safety checklist with AI and check it against the manual or an official safety source, adding anything AI missed before the work starts.
Many trade and warehouse jobs use a job safety (or hazard) analysis: list the steps of a job, the hazards at each step, and how to control them. Example hazards: falls, electrical shock, lifting injuries, moving equipment like forklifts, chemicals and heat.
AI can draft one: "Make a job safety checklist for replacing a ceiling light fixture: steps, hazards and controls, including personal protective equipment." It will often include good basics like turning off the breaker and testing that power is off.
But AI is not a safety authority. Check the list with your supervisor, the manufacturer's instructions and official sources such as OSHA (osha.gov). OSHA 10-hour and 30-hour Outreach classes teach safety basics; OSHA says the card is voluntary and is not a certification or license, though some employers and states require it.
Step by step:
- List the job's steps.
- Ask AI for hazards and controls at each step, including protective equipment.
- Check it with your supervisor, the manual and osha.gov.
- Fix anything missing or wrong.
- Review it with the crew before starting.
Words to know:
- Hazard: something that could hurt someone.
- PPE: personal protective equipment, like gloves, safety glasses, hard hats and steel-toe boots.
- Job safety analysis: a list of a job's steps, hazards and controls.
Official sources:
- OSHA Outreach Training Program
- OSHA Outreach Training Program FAQs
Try it now: Ask AI for a job safety checklist for one real task (like lifting heavy boxes or changing a tire). Then find one official safety page or the manual for that task and add anything AI missed.
You can now draft a job safety checklist with AI and check it against official sources.

check.q: What three things does a job safety analysis list?
options: Steps, hazards and controls
Tools, prices and times
Workers, shifts and breaks
Customers, addresses and phone numbers
check.why: A job safety analysis lists each step, its hazards and the controls for them.

check.q: Your AI safety checklist for lifting boxes does not mention gloves, but the employer's rule requires them. What would you do?
options: Leave gloves off because AI did not list them
Ask AI again until it agrees
Add gloves to the checklist and follow the employer's rule
Wear gloves only on heavy boxes
check.why: Official and employer rules win; add what AI missed.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Keeping a work log with photos and notes
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Keep a daily work log with photos and short notes, using AI to tidy them.
This lesson builds toward: After a job, you will write a work log entry with date, location, work done, materials, issues, next steps and photo notes, with every part included and no private customer information.
A good work log protects you and impresses employers: it shows what you did, when, and that it was done right. Take before-and-after photos, note materials used, problems found, and time spent.
Use voice-to-text on your phone to talk your notes at the end of a job, then ask AI: "Turn these notes into a short, professional work log entry with date, location, work done, materials, issues and next steps." Check it is accurate.
Follow your employer's rules about photos: some sites do not allow photos, and you should never photograph customers, their private papers or security systems without permission. Store logs where your employer says.
Step by step:
- Take before-and-after photos where allowed.
- Speak or type quick notes at the end of the job.
- Ask AI to format a work log entry.
- Check it for accuracy.
- Save it where your employer says.
Words to know:
- Work log: a daily record of the work you did.
- Voice-to-text: a phone feature that turns your speech into written words.
Try it now: Do a small job at home (fix, clean or organize something). Take before-and-after photos, speak your notes, and have AI turn them into a work log entry.
You can now keep a professional work log with photos and AI-tidied notes.

check.q: What does a before photo in a work log show?
options: How fast you worked
The condition before you started the job
The customer's face
Your tools for sale
check.why: Before and after photos show what you changed and that it was done right.

check.q: A customer's bank statement is on the counter where you are working. What would you do before taking a photo?
options: Take the photo; it is only for the log
Ask AI if it is okay
Zoom in on the statement so it is clear
Move out of frame or ask the customer to move it
check.why: Do not photograph private papers without permission.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Planning routes, loads and inventory
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Use map apps and AI to plan a route and a simple load or inventory list.
This lesson builds toward: Given several stops or items, you will plan a route and a simple load or inventory list, then check the route in a map app, with loads in reverse stop order and drive times checked.
Delivery drivers, service techs and warehouse workers plan routes and loads every day. Free map apps like Google Maps let you add several stops and show traffic. Many companies use their own routing software; learn it when you start.
AI can help you think it through: "I have 6 service calls: [areas and time windows]. Suggest an order that saves driving and meets the time windows." Then check it in the map app. For loads: "Make a loading list for these deliveries so the last stop's items go in first."
For inventory, a simple sheet with item, location (aisle, shelf), quantity and reorder point helps. Never let AI override weight limits, load securement rules, or hours-of-service rules for drivers; those come from your employer and official transportation rules.
Step by step:
- List stops with areas and time windows.
- Ask AI to suggest an order.
- Check it in a map app with traffic.
- Make a load list: last stop loaded first.
- Follow weight, securement and driving-hours rules from your employer.
Words to know:
- Route: the order and path of stops.
- Load securement: tying down cargo so it cannot shift or fall.
- Hours of service: rules limiting how long commercial drivers can drive and work.
Try it now: Pick five real places in your area. Ask AI to suggest the best order to visit them, then check it in a free map app and compare drive times.
You can now plan a route and load with AI and map apps while following the rules.

options: A list of what you have in stock and how many
The fastest route
A driver's hours
A safety rule for loading
check.why: Inventory is a count of the items you have.

check.q: AI suggests a route order for five stops. What would you do next?
options: Follow it without looking
Check it in a map app with traffic before you drive
Ask the customers to choose
Drive to the farthest stop first
check.why: AI route ideas need checking in a map app with current traffic.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Finding apprenticeships and trade jobs
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Find a registered apprenticeship or trade job and prepare to apply.
This lesson builds toward: Using Apprenticeship.gov or a local program, you will find one apprenticeship or trade job you could apply for, and write down its requirements and how to apply.
A Registered Apprenticeship lets you earn a paycheck while you learn a trade, with classroom training and a recognized credential at the end. The U.S. Department of Labor's Apprenticeship.gov has an Apprenticeship Job Finder. Unions, community colleges and pre-apprenticeship programs also offer paths.
Ask AI to explain a trade: "What does an HVAC apprentice do day to day, what tools do they use, and what math is involved?" Then ask it to help turn your experience into a trade résumé, keeping everything true.
Some trades and driving jobs need licenses, tests or a clean driving record, and some licenses consider criminal records; check your state licensing agency and ask your reentry or workforce program which employers and programs welcome people with records. Show up reliable and ready to learn: in trades, that matters most.
Step by step:
- Search Apprenticeship.gov's job finder and local union or college programs.
- Ask AI to explain the trade and the skills it needs.
- Check license and record rules with your state agency.
- Ask your reentry or workforce program for fair-chance employers.
- Build a true trade résumé with AI help.
Words to know:
- Registered Apprenticeship: a paid job with training that leads to a recognized credential.
- Pre-apprenticeship: a short program that prepares you to enter an apprenticeship.
- Journeyworker: a fully trained worker in a trade.
Official sources:
- Apprenticeship.gov (U.S. Department of Labor)
Try it now: Final task: search Apprenticeship.gov or a local program for one apprenticeship or trade job you could apply for. Then finish your job packet: manual summary, estimate or work order, checked safety checklist, work log entry and route or load plan.
You can now use AI to work smarter in a trade or logistics job and find a path into one.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Manual summary The summary has a number that does not match the manual, or no source. Plain-language summary with every number checked against the manual. Also notes which step needs a supervisor or a licensed worker. Estimate or work order Missing labor, parts, total, what is included or the expiry date, or the math is wrong. All parts are there and the math is checked by hand. Also says what is not included and how changes will be approved. Safety checklist Copied from AI with no official check. Checked against the manual or an official source, with anything missing added. Names the source and the PPE for each hazard. Work log Missing date, work done, materials, issues or next steps, or shows private information. A complete entry with before-and-after photo notes and no private information. Another worker could pick up the job from this entry alone. Route or load plan Route not checked, or the load is in the wrong order. Route checked in a map app and loads placed in reverse stop order. Also lists inventory counts and notes rules from the employer. Next job found No apprenticeship or job found. One real apprenticeship or trade job with its requirements and how to apply. Also lists the first step they will take this week. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

options: A license to work alone
A paid job as a supervisor
A program that prepares you to enter an apprenticeship
A test you take after an apprenticeship
check.why: A pre-apprenticeship builds the basics so you can get into an apprenticeship.

check.q: You want to know if a trade license you need considers a criminal record. What would you do?
options: Guess based on a friend's story
Ask AI and trust its answer
Give up on that trade
Check with your state licensing agency
check.why: The state licensing agency has the official rules for that license.
